chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Ali ibn Ri'ab and Hisham ibn al-Salim, on the authority of Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the four winds: the North, the South, the East (Dubur), and the West (Saba). And I said to him, 'The people mention that the North is from Paradise, and the South is from Hell.' He said, 'Indeed, for Allah, the Exalted, are troops of winds with which He chastises whom He pleases among those who disobey Him, and for each of these winds is an angel appointed over it. When Allah, the Exalted, wishes to chastise a people with a type of chastisement, He inspires the angel appointed over that type of wind which He intends to chastise them with. He said: 'The angel commands it, and it roars like a roaring lion.' And for each of these winds is a name. Do you not hear His, the Exalted's, saying: "The 'Aad denied, so how [terrible] was My penalty and warning"? And He mentioned winds in the chastisement. Then He said: 'The wind of the North, and the wind of the West, and the wind of the South, and the wind of the East are also attributed to the angels appointed over them.'

key_terms.الرِّيَاح الْأَرْبَع: The four winds (North, South, East, West)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of the four winds in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the four winds are not inherently from Paradise or Hell but serve as divine 'troops' commanded by specific angels to chastise the disobedient, linking natural phenomena directly to God's will. This narration emphasizes the angelic agency behind meteorological events, citing Quranic examples where winds were instruments of punishment for nations like 'Ad. The text affirms that each wind has a designated angelic ruler, reinforcing the Shia understanding of the interconnectedness of the physical and spiritual realms in executing divine decree.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-138 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Ali ibn Re’ab and Hisham ibn Salim, on the authority of Abi Basir, “

I asked Aba Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) regarding the four winds: the North wind; the South wind; the Eurus wind from the East ; and the Zephyr wind from the West . I told him, ‘The people say that the North wind blows from Paradise and the South wind blows from Hell. He (MGB) replied, ‘The Honorable the Exalted God has troops of winds with which He chastises the disobedient ones which He pleases to chastise. An angel is appointed to each wind. Whenever the Honorable the Exalted God wishes to impose a certain form of chastisement to a nation, He would inspire that appointed angel with what kind of chastisement He wants to be imposed upon them. The angel would issue an order to the wind to blow and the wind will roar like a lion. Each wind has a name. Consider what the Honorable the Exalted God said, ‘The Ad (people) (too) rejected (Truth): then how terrible was My Penalty and My Warning?’ And God mentions a wind to torture them as we read, ‘For We sent against them a furious wind, on a Day of violent Disaster, plucking out men as if they were roots of palm-trees torn up (from the ground).’ When the people talk of the North wind, the South wind, the Eurus or the Zephyr, they ascribe these winds to their appointed angels.’”
